title: Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum
one_line: Across 60+ futures (equities, bonds, commodities, FX) 1974-2020, the return from the previous close to the last half hour predicts the last 30 minutes' return, and the effect reverts over the next days; the authors link it to short-gamma hedging by option dealers and leveraged ETFs.

findings.statement: The return from the previous close up to the last half hour positively predicts the last-30-minute return.
findings.evidence: Economically and statistically significant across 60+ futures, 1974-2020 (Journal of Financial Economics 142(1), 2021).

findings.statement: The effect reverts over the following days.
Intraday momentum is linked to hedging of short-gamma positions by option market makers and leveraged ETFs.
findings.evidence: Hedging short gamma requires trading in the direction of the price move.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics of forced players (short-gamma dealers, leveraged-ETF rebalancing) near the close.
why.mechanism: Short-gamma hedgers must buy after rallies and sell after drops, mostly near the close; the push scales with the day's move.
why.who_is_forced: Option dealers net short gamma; leveraged/inverse ETFs rebalancing daily.
why.what_would_kill_it: Dealers moving net long gamma (heavy overwriting, 0DTE dynamics), shrinking leveraged-ETF AUM.

reported_results.headline: Rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes; reverts over the next days.

tradable_edge: Covered by the existing spec noise_area_last_half_hour_es (this paper is its WHY) — its baseline B2 (direction of the day's move into 15:30, no band) is exactly this paper's signal.
angles: Already in the last-30-minutes sheet as baseline B2

decay_risk.reason: Long sample, structural flows; but 0DTE since 2022 may change dealer gamma near the close.
